new_findings.expected_impact: Explains 100% of this session's launch failures; blocks everything downstream of import.
new_findings.source: runs/baseline/2fc18296.../server.log; /opt/envs/wu1w/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/cuda/__init__.py:833-860; Magpie/modes/benchmark/benchmarker.py:776,800; reproduced in-session: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3 ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -c 'import vllm' -> same RuntimeError
new_findings.what: ROOT CAUSE of the 'unknown' launch failure is NOT a model gap. Magpie composes the server env as os.environ.copy() overlaid with benchmark.envs (_build_local_command, benchmarker.py:776/800). benchmark.envs pins ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 for TP=1 but never HIP/CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, so the harness-inherited PHYSICAL HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES (observed '2' live; '2,3' in the 13:50 baseline log) survives into the vllm child. torch._parse_visible_devices() hard-raises when len(HIP)>len(ROCR), and vLLM triggers it during 'import vllm' (env_override -> torch.cuda.is_available()). The process therefore dies before binding a port, so no model-side error exists to classify -> the empty/unknown failure_kind signature.

A fix that merely satisfies torch's length check (pinning HIP to a same-length PHYSICAL id) passes validation and then dies later and less legibly. Only the LOGICAL 0..n-1 index is correct, because ROCR filters at the HSA agent layer and re-indexes what survives.

Counts are equal, so torch._parse_visible_devices() passes and vLLM binds the socket, then EngineCore dies deeper and illegibly at worker init_device -> torch.accelerator.set_device_index -> torch._C._cuda_init() -> 'RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available'. Control (same leaked env, no delta) = that exact traceback + 'Process died before http://0.0.0.0:8932/health became ready'; candidate (only extra_envs HIP/CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0) = status SUCCESS, /health 200, inferencex_result.json produced.

new_findings.expected_impact: Prevents a future round from proposing unset_envs or 'just unset HIP', which look correct but are provably inert against an inherited var.
new_findings.what: Only one config mechanism can fix the leak, and the obvious alternative cannot. A variant's extra_envs is written into benchmark.envs, which Magpie applies OVER an os.environ.copy() in _build_local_command (benchmarker.py:776 'env = os.environ.copy()', then :800 'for key, value in env_vars.items(): env[key] = str(value)') -> it DOES override an inherited leak. unset_envs only pops the key from the YAML dict (_grid_runner.py:664-669), after which Magpie re-adds the inherited value from os.environ -> it CANNOT remove an inherited var. Simply removing HIP does not work either: the InferenceX launcher derives HIP from ROCR only under '[ -z "$HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES" ]' (vllm_mi300x.sh:65-68), which an inherited value defeats. HIP must therefore be SET to a value via extra_envs.

new_findings.expected_impact: Makes the enablement delta robust to whichever mask the harness leaks, instead of trading one failure mode for another.
new_findings.what: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES must be set TOGETHER and EQUAL, so the delta is atomic. vLLM's _sync_hip_cuda_env_vars() runs at import, raises a hard ValueError on any HIP/CUDA disagreement, and copies an inherited CUDA value onto HIP when HIP is unset. A one-sided pin (HIP=0 while CUDA leaks a physical id) converts a device-selection bug into an import-time crash. Validated empirically: the successful boot had ROCR=0 + HIP=0 + CUDA=0 all set, emitting only the benign 'Using CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES on ROCm is deprecated' warning.

proposal_set.reason: Makes the combo boot. The harness inherits HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 (a PHYSICAL id) while the gate config pins ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; ROCR filters at the HSA layer and re-indexes survivors to 0..n-1, so HIP must carry the LOGICAL index. Because the counts are equal, torch's length check passes and the failure lands deep and illegibly: EngineCore 'RuntimeError: No CUDA GPUs are available' at init_device. PROVEN by A/B on the real Magpie/InferenceX gate path under the identical inherited leak and with the kept patch NOT applied: control reproduced the crash, this delta alone yielded status SUCCESS, /health 200 and a produced inferencex_result.json (110.19 tok/s on a deliberately reduced 8-prompt/conc=4 config used only to keep the proof fast - NOT a baseline-comparable number). extra_envs rather than unset_envs is required: unset only pops the YAML dict while Magpie re-adds the inherited value from os.environ, and the launcher's '[ -z HIP ]' derivation cannot fire on an inherited value. Both vars are pinned equal and together because vLLM raises ValueError on a HIP/CUDA disagreement and copies an inherited CUDA onto HIP. Scoped to TP=1 (this session's fixed TP), where the logical set is exactly {0}; mirrors Magpie's own documented gpu_selection rule (benchmarker.py:519-522).

new_findings.what: WHY THE PRIOR ROUND'S FIX DID NOT HOLD — two verified reasons, and they explain the whole stall_streak. (1) The accepted env pin never reached the BASELINE launch. Verified semantics: HIP/CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES are in GPU_MASK_ENV_NAMES (hyperloom/common/visible_devices.py:96) which is ORed into BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_ENV_NAMES (common/env_safety.py:286-289, used by remote-recipe/framework-switch sanitisation) but are NOT in BLOCKED_VARIANT_ENV_NAMES, so is_allowed_variant_env_key('HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES') == True and the materializer would keep them if handed. Decisive artefact: they were NOT handed to the two failing baseline attempts — runs/baseline/48e0ae2b(15:14)/baseline_config.with_envs.yaml and 0668d71b(15:51)/... both render `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES: '0'` with NO HIP/CUDA key, while baseline.py:3519 takes them only from params['extra_envs']. The grid path does apply a variant's extra_envs unfiltered (_grid_runner.py:670), which is exactly why the prior round's own rebench SUCCEEDED while the gate's baseline kept failing: the fix was only ever wired into the variant path, and the gate is sealed against the baseline. A source-level fix in the layer both paths share is therefore required, not another env pin. (2) The kept Magpie patch is not permanent: integrate_patch backs up the target (patch_backups/*__0000.bak) and restores it on REVERT, so grep -c _reconcile_rocm_device_masks /opt/envs/vllm/.../Magpie/modes/benchmark/benchmarker.py == 0 right now — the tree is unpatched again.

new_findings.what: AUTHORED AND PROVEN: patches/002_reconcile_inherited_device_masks.patch (165 lines, +129/-0, `git apply --check` PASS against the live /opt/envs/vllm/lib/python3.12/site-packages tree). It adds reconcile_rocm_device_masks() to hyperloom/orchestrator/actions/executors/_workload_envs.py — the single layer that OWNS the ROCR pin and that EVERY launch path (baseline.py:3528, integrate_patch.py:4503, explore/grid) traverses, so unlike a variant extra_envs it cannot be scrubbed — and calls it (i) immediately after the TP-derived ROCR write, (ii) once more at the final sink before yaml.safe_dump, plus a call in _grid_runner.py after the variant extra_envs merge so an explicit variant pin is honoured and then validated. The key design point: the leak lives in the PARENT os.environ, not in the YAML, so the helper reads `envs` first and falls back to os.environ, and WRITES the corrected logical 0..N-1 mask into benchmark.envs (which Magpie overlays on os.environ.copy() at Magpie/modes/benchmark/benchmarker.py:776,800) so it overrides the inherited carve. It is conservative: inert off ROCm (no /dev/kfd or /sys/module/amdgpu), inert with no effective ROCR mask, inert when the mask already validly indexes the ROCR set (an intentional TP=2 multi-card launch stays 2-wide), it never modifies/removes ROCR, it leaves UUID masks to the runtime, and it is wrapped in a blanket try/except so env hygiene can never itself break a launch.
